formula:
proxy_return = opportunity * (0.35 + 0.65 * channel_attention_share)

opportunity =
    0.40 * minmax(log(internet_users))
  + 0.25 * minmax(internet_user_cagr)
  + 0.20 * minmax(share of population ages 0-14)
  + 0.15 * (1 - minmax(log(gdp_per_capita_usd)))

internet_users = population * (internet users % / 100) on the latest year
where both World Bank series are present. CAGR uses that constructed series
from the earliest to the latest overlapping year, and only if the span is at
least 3 years.

Ages 0-14 stand in for a youth audience because the World Bank API rejected
the 15-24 indicator id SP.POP.1524.TO.ZS. It is not the 15-24 music demographic.

If CAGR or the age share is missing for any eligible market, that component is
dropped and the remaining weights are renormalized to 1. A market is eligible
only when internet_users and gdp_per_capita are both positive.

channel_attention_share is the last-12-month share of local-Wikipedia
pageviews among streaming DSP, short video, and social/influencer articles.
It is an attention proxy, not a measured return. If the share is missing, the
row has no proxy label and is not used for training.

Min-max is fit on the eligible markets in the same run only. The result is a
unitless index, not revenue per dollar and not an NLS profit figure.
why_xgboost: XGBoost is the estimator because the training table is a few dozen rows. Depth-wise trees with max_depth 2 and a large L2 penalty stay shallower than LightGBM's leaf-wise default, which will isolate single markets on a sample this small. Either library would be underpowered; XGBoost is the more constrained default and installs as a single wheel. This is not a claim that gradient boosting recovers real promo ROI from public covariates.

limitations: The training label is a documented formula, not NLS campaign profit or loss.
Leave-one-market-out on seven markets is a small sample. The metrics move if one market is unusual.
Language-edition Wikipedia pageviews are not streaming MAU and are not a clean country panel.
No public sync rate card or territory CPM/CPC series entered the model.
Ages 0-14 stand in for a youth audience. The 15-24 World Bank indicator id was rejected by the API.
Mobile, broadband, and server density still correlate with income and internet use, so some fit is mechanical.
Confidence is capped at 0.85 because the label is synthetic.
Apple charts are one snapshot, not a growth series.
Hong Kong mobile subscriptions per 100 people exceed 300 because of multi-SIM use. The indie score caps that input at 150.
Output is a research allocation of a proxy index, not media-buying advice.
